messages.subject: MCMC chain of log(L)
parts:
I would like to get a vector of log(L) values for each iteration of the MCMC. It seems that I should be able to do that with getLogProbNodes(), but I cannot figure out how exactly.

I would greatly appreciate any guidance.

Thanks a lot.

Cheers,
Brook

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: MCMC chain of log(L)
parts:
Brook, your email is well-timed.  There's a new feature under development, which does precisely that.

Are you able to install nimble from a developmental branch?  You can do so using the code below:

remove.packages('nimble')
library(remotes)
remotes::install_github('nimble-dev/nimble', ref = 'derived_quantities', subdir = 'packages/nimble')
library(nimble)

If that worked, then you can do exactly as you asked ("get a vector of log(L) values for each iteration of the MCMC"), using nimbleMCMC, as:

out <- nimbleMCMC(...., logProb = TRUE)

After that, the (summed) log(L) for the entire model will be available in:

out$derived$logProb

There is more fine grained control available also, if you only want the log(L) for certain sets of nodes.  If that's your goal, let me know, and we can discuss further.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: MCMC chain of log(L)
parts:
Good question, Luca.  Using this option, MCMC sampling will proceed exactly as it has in the past.  And none of the log-density values are ever *recalculated*, but rather the values are simply extracted from the model object.  So, without having done any formal comparisons, my instinct is to say not much slower at all.

If you have time to conduct any experiments or testing of this, I would be most happy to hear what you find.

Also, if you encounter any errors or unexpected behaviour, please do let me know.

Cheers,
Daniel
